contents.name: Theorem 17.11 with Theorems 6.21 and 6.26
contents.support: Under countable choice, first establish the following local smoothing construction on the boundaryless manifolds of this page. Given continuous F:P→N smooth on an open V containing closed A, embed N properly by j into R^k. The Euclidean tubular diffeomorphism E gives an open U containing j(N) and smooth retraction r=π∘E^{-1} via the normal-bundle projection. Set e(p)=min(1,dist(jF(p),U^c)/2) if U^c is nonempty, and e=1 otherwise. Distance to a nonempty closed set is finite and 1-Lipschitz by the triangle inequality; openness gives positive distance at each jF(p). Hence e is positive continuous and B_e(jF(p)) lies in U. Absolute Euclidean Whitney gives smooth Q with |Q-jF|<e. Construct the cutoff from a subordinate refinement-indexed smooth partition (φ_i) for {V,P\A}, not an assumed two-function output. Assign each support to V if possible, and to P\A otherwise; this is a prescribed two-case rule. Let χ be the sum of the V-assigned functions. Both grouped sums are locally finite smooth sums. Each grouped union of closed supports is closed: near any point only finitely many supports occur, so its complement is locally the complement of a finite closed union. Consequently suppχ is contained in V, while the other grouped support union is closed and disjoint from A. On its open complement χ=1, giving the required neighbourhood of A. Put R=χjF+(1-χ)Q. This is smooth on V and equals Q on a neighbourhood of each point outside suppχ, so is globally smooth. It equals jF near A and |R-jF|=(1-χ)|Q-jF|<e. Therefore G=j^{-1}rR is smooth, agrees with F near A, and j^{-1}r((1-s)jF+sR) is a continuous homotopy F~G rel A, since the entire segment stays in the e-ball. For a continuous homotopy H between smooth f0,f1 set P=M×R, λ(t)=σ(3t-1) using the standard step, F(x,t)=H(x,λ(t)), V=M×((−∞,1/3)∪(2/3,∞)), and A=M×((−∞,1/4]∪[3/4,∞)). F is smooth on V. The construction gives a smooth map on M×R with the exact endpoint collars; restriction to[0,1] and smooth homotopy invariance give equal de Rham maps. Taking A empty and χ=0 also gives a smooth representative of every continuous map, with the explicit straight-line retraction homotopy. For continuous inverse homotopy equivalences f,g, smooth them to f',g'; composition and concatenation give g'f'~id and f'g'~id, and the endpoint construction smooths these homotopies. Thus pullbacks are inverse algebra maps; two smooth representatives of one continuous class likewise induce the same map. Empty sources are immediate, and a map to an empty target forces an empty source. Countable choice covers countable coordinate/partition/approximation/tubular selections; no relative Whitney theorem, continuous-map smoothing corollary or fine-tubular-radius lemma is used. For the countable-choice implementation of the partition suppliers, use the set of all admissible coordinate-ball tuples instead of choosing one tuple for every point. Second countability and countable choice give the needed countable subcover and tuple representatives. In the shrinking proof take each exhaustion index to be the least suitable integer; on each compact annulus take all admissible nested pairs, and use countable choice on the countable family of nonempty sets of finite subcovers, then on the countable family of bump choices. Flatten the supplied finite lists and normalize the locally finite bump sum as in the published partition construction. Thus no uncountable pointwise choice or dependent recursive selection is hidden. The current local tube proof uses capped eligible radii, proves supremum-endpoint injectivity and 1-Lipschitz continuity, and constructs the retraction from an injective local diffeomorphism; it does not consume the defective smooth-minorant or global tubular-existence proof. The actual embedding supplier is now the published locally repaired finite-dimensional (bounded G, proper rho) theorem under CC, with full compact-band projections/gluing; the dimension-optimal weak Whitney theorem is no longer consumed. Fresh independent scaffold review remains required.

canonical.name: A degenerate pullback metric under a constant map
canonical.support: For a constant map F:M→R from a smooth manifold of dimension n>0, the pullback F*(dx²) is zero. It is not Riemannian exactly when M is nonempty; for M empty it is vacuously a Riemannian metric. In particular F:R→R, F(x)=0 gives a degenerate pullback.
canonical.proof_plan: The differential of a constant coordinate expression is zero, so the pullback tensor vanishes. If M is nonempty, choose one point and one chart; its first coordinate tangent vector is nonzero since n>0 and has zero quadratic value. If M is empty there are no tangent vectors at points to test, so smoothness and positive definiteness are vacuous. The concrete source R supplies the required counterexample without choice.
